clue.text: Bad luck with mousetrap

definitions.meaning: a British exclamation of mock sympathy meaning tough luck
mousetrap is slang for cheap, dry, unappetising cheddar of the sort used to bait traps

explanation.definitionFit: A British idiom for misfortune, and literally the tough cheese nicknamed after the bait in a trap.

clue.text: It's time I split from beautiful woman

indicators.note: split from means the letter I breaks away from the word that follows

parts.note: a houri is a beautiful young woman, originally one of the maidens of the Muslim paradise

explanation.surface: A man announces it is time to break up with his gorgeous girlfriend.
explanation.definitionFit: Sixty minutes is a unit of time, so the word names a measure of time.

clue.text: Earlier capital diplomacy used to deal with unrest

parts.note: Rio de Janeiro was Brazil's capital before Brasilia
tact is diplomacy, skill in handling people

explanation.surface: A former seat of government once relied on diplomacy to calm its rioting citizens.
explanation.walkthrough: The Riot Act was an old British law read aloud to order a crowd to disperse; to read someone the riot act is to rebuke them.
explanation.definitionFit: The historic statute was read to rioters to quell disorder, so it was the instrument for dealing with unrest.

clue.text: less three will fail

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held reads only 'less three will fail' (4,2,6), cut short at the start; the scan is blank and a search of the exact text found nothing.

clue.text: Guarantee criticism won't start

indicators.note: won't start means the word loses its opening letter

parts.note: censure is strong criticism or disapproval

explanation.surface: Someone promises that no criticism will be launched.
explanation.definitionFit: To guarantee something is to make certain of it, a straight synonym.

clue.text: Came to blows —- second blow was first …

parts.note: a cuff is a blow with the open hand
to have led is to have been first, at the front

explanation.surface: A report on a fight: someone got in a second punch after landing the first.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue runs on, by the dots, into 7-down, but each half is a complete clue of its own.
explanation.definitionFit: To scuffle is to fight confusedly at close quarters, so it means came to blows.

clue.text: Neighbour turns into a music-maker

indicators.note: turns tells us to read the verb for neighbour back to front

parts.note: to neighbour something is to abut it, to lie next to it

explanation.surface: A next-door resident takes up playing an instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Neighbour' reads as a noun but is the verb, meaning to lie alongside.
explanation.definitionFit: The large low brass instrument is a maker of music in a band or orchestra.

clue.text: … from German and therefore put up with

parts.note: und is the German word for and
ergo is Latin for therefore

explanation.surface: Continuing from 5-down, a fighter from Germany had to endure the consequences.
explanation.definitionFit: To undergo hardship is to endure or suffer it, so it means put up with.

clue.text: Available for immediate use, they're a tad different

indicators.note: different signals that the letters of these words are rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone observes that a set of items is slightly unusual.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: something held ready to be used at once, like a weapon prepared for firing.

clue.text: Goodness! No lumps! You'll be confused

indicators.note: be confused, joined with the 'll of you'll as will be confused, says the letters are jumbled

parts.note: the word you supplies its letters, its 'll reading as will before be confused

explanation.surface: A cook promises a lump-free sauce that will baffle the diners.
explanation.definitionFit: An old-fashioned exclamation of surprise, used just as goodness! is.

clue.text: Arrange return of water

indicators.note: return of means the word for water is turned round to run backwards

parts.note: the tide is the sea's water rising and falling

explanation.surface: Someone organises for the tide to come back in.
explanation.definitionFit: To edit material is to arrange and prepare it for publication, a looser synonym.

clue.text: Sorrow expressed over crow's bloomer

indicators.note: over in a down clue places the first part above the second
expressed means the word for sorrow is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: mourning is sorrow for the dead
to glory, as in glory in, is to exult or crow

explanation.surface: Someone voices grief at a crow's mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomer' tempts as a blunder, but it is a flowering plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A bloomer is anything that blooms; this climbing plant has trumpet flowers that open in the early part of the day.

clue.text: Route some craft botched — it's only to be expected

indicators.note: botched means made a mess of, so these letters are put together badly in a new order

explanation.surface: A trip is ruined by poor boats, which is no surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for something natural and expected, not worth remarking on.

clue.text: Like a computer to choose man in charge

parts.note: to elect is to choose, especially by vote
Ron is a man's name

explanation.surface: A recommendation to pick a boss.
explanation.definitionFit: A computer works with electronic circuits, so the adjective describes it.

clue.text: Set fire to some petitions

parts.note: lit is the past tense of light, to set fire to
any can mean some, as in have you any

explanation.surface: Protesters burn a few of the petitions.
explanation.definitionFit: A litany is a series of prayers or petitions recited in church.

clue.text: Support for runner, a lanky fellow

definitions.meaning: a tall pole that a climbing bean, here the runner bean, grows up
an informal name for a tall, thin person

explanation.definitionFit: Literally the stick a climbing plant grows on, and figuratively a tall skinny person.

clue.text: A tree was pickled in brine

indicators.note: pickled, as in steeped in brine or drunk, says the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A tree has been preserved in salt water.
explanation.definitionFit: Brine is salt water, and the sea is the commonest source of it.

clue.text: Roundabout where vehicle collided with bird

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
the ousel, or ouzel, is a thrush, such as the blackbird or ring ousel

explanation.surface: A car hit a bird at a traffic roundabout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Collided with' only joins the two pieces. A roundabout is British for a traffic circle; the definition is the fairground ride.
explanation.definitionFit: A carousel is a merry-go-round, which British English also calls a roundabout.

clue.text: Produce an own goal, perhaps -— tied again?

definitions.meaning: to bounce back off something, as a ball may deflect off a defender into their own net

explanation.definitionFit: A ball that bounces back may go in off a defender, and split as re-bound it means tied once more.

clue.text: Wrongful detention of goods endlessly returned by cooperative

indicators.note: returned means the shortened legal term is written backwards
endlessly means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: detinue is the legal action for the wrongful keeping of another's goods

explanation.surface: A legal note: goods unlawfully held are finally handed back by a cooperative.
explanation.definitionFit: A united effort is a cooperative one, people working together.

clue.text: Rough path round state is hard work

indicators.note: round means the path goes around the abbreviation for the state

parts.note: a trail is a rough path
VA is the abbreviation for Virginia, a US state

explanation.surface: A rough track around a region makes for heavy going.
explanation.definitionFit: Travail is painful or laborious effort, so it means hard work.

clue.text: Temper frequently overcome by saint

indicators.note: overcome by in a down clue puts the second word beneath the first, so the saint sits on top

parts.note: often means frequently

explanation.surface: A bad temper is often conquered by a saintly person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Temper' looks like a noun, anger, but it is the verb, to moderate.
explanation.definitionFit: To temper something is to moderate it, which is to soften it.

clue.text: Inefficient masseur might get someone's back up

definitions.meaning: an unskilled masseur might stroke the muscles in the wrong direction
an idiom for annoying or irritating someone

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for irritating someone comes from stroking a cat's fur against its lie, the literal sense here.

clue.text: Cavity covered by fancy stitching

indicators.note: covered by says the answer lies concealed inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A hole has been hidden under some decorative needlework.
explanation.definitionFit: A cyst is a sac or cavity in the body, usually filled with fluid.

clue.text: Part of speech made by someone in order to cover up nothing

indicators.note: to cover up means the religious woman's letters wrap around the zero

parts.note: a nun is a member of a religious order
O, the figure zero, means nothing

explanation.surface: A grammarian works out how to conceal a void.
explanation.definitionFit: A noun is one of the parts of speech, a naming word.

clue.text: Parking place by a line

parts.note: a station is a place or post where someone is put
RY is the abbreviation for railway, a line

explanation.surface: A spot to park beside a road marking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Parking' looks like a noun, but here it is the adjective sense, as in a vehicle that is parked.
explanation.definitionFit: A parked vehicle is not moving, so the adjective for standing still fits.

clue.text: Coleridge's first poem — it's difficult to read

indicators.note: first means take only the opening letter of the poet's name

parts.note: an ode is a lyric poem

explanation.surface: Coleridge's earliest poem is hard going.
explanation.walkthrough: Samuel Taylor Coleridge was an English Romantic poet.
explanation.definitionFit: A message in code cannot be read without the key, so it is hard to read.

clue.text: The old part of the house?

definitions.text: The old part of the house?

parts.words: The old part of the house?
parts.note: a section of a home set aside for an elderly relative, read as the portion of the house for an old person

explanation.definitionFit: A self-contained flat attached to a family home, for an elderly relative to live in.
